boredom noun

also tedium, weariness

classical

Sall. Jug. 62.9; Liv. 8.2.2; Quint. 2.2.6 (Lewis & Short)
Andresian p. 36

taedium, taediī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

weariness, tedium

Weariness of a thing, with the genitive (taedium labōris); Lewis & Short notes it is rare before Augustus and perhaps not in Cicero or Caesar. For “I’m bored” the verb taedet is commoner (see be bored).

Examples

  • taediō cūrārum fessus

    worn out with the weariness of his caresTac. Ann. 12.39

See also be bored.

SourcesLewis & Short: taedium

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 36.
